Restaurant's own Popmenu site (pacificpizza.net/menu) server-renders only a 9-item 'popular' sample via window.POPMENU_APOLLO_STATE, not the full catalog; full items are client-fetched via GraphQL. The sampled 14" Medium Pizza price ($14) disagrees with both the Slice/DoorDash list ($22.80) and the previously-derived 1.2x base ($19) -- a three-way disagreement, not corroboration. No dine-in artefact (PDF, photo, printed menu) found. Needs either a browser to page through the Popmenu GraphQL-backed tabs, or a photographed/PDF menu.
notes: Class of obstacle: markup-tainted ordering channels plus an own-site sample too small to use, not a dead end -- a browser or a menu photo would likely finish this in one pass.

blocked: No first-party website (work list has none, and none found by search). DoorDash marketplace (91 items, address confirmed 1766 North Coast Highway 101) shows odd non-.99 cents (e.g. $9.06, $16.88, $19.36, $8.74) that divide cleanly onto typical .99/.49/.00-ending base prices at a 1.25x divisor for 63-83 of 91 items depending on strictness -- consistent with a ~25% markup, not organic pricing. allmenus.com has a full 115-item priced listing that could serve as a second source, but its prices run 2x+ below DoorDash on matching items (e.g. Carne Asada Burrito $6.99 on allmenus vs $16.88 on DoorDash) -- per the staleness rule a 2x+ gap is an old snapshot, not a markup match, so allmenus cannot corroborate or replace the DoorDash figures.
notes: Class of obstacle: only a marked-up marketplace source and a stale directory listing, no first-party site or dine-in artefact. A dated Yelp menu photo or a phone call to the restaurant would settle this.

name: Main Street Coffee
blocked: Restaurant's own site (mainstreetcoffeeramona.com/menu/) lists only category descriptions, no per-item prices or a PDF -- 'Order Here' points to main-street-coffee-llc.square.site (Square Online). That storefront's initial HTML (window.__BOOTSTRAP_STATE__) carries only site/theme config, no catalog items or prices; /s/order, /menu, /shop all client-redirect back to the SPA shell with nothing server-rendered. This is the named Square Online case in the playbook -- genuinely needs a browser. Yelp 403s a bare curl (no browser available to check for a dated menu photo).
notes: Class of obstacle: client-side-only Square Online ordering SPA, needs a browser to watch network traffic for the catalog fetch.

notes: Class of obstacle: only one usable source at the lowest ladder tier, needs a second independent priced source (a DoorDash/Grubhub-app search from a browser, or a Yelp/FB menu photo) to clear the two-source bar.

name: Tandoor
blocked: Confirmed via re-fetch: tandoorsandiego.com is still the same Flash-era (2008-2012) site at 5608 Mission Center Road, San Diego (matches work list address). Its menu.html still prices vegetable samosas at $2.99, whole wheat naan at $2.29, palak paneer combination at $6.99/a la carte $5.89, lamb curry combination $13.99 -- the exact stale price level FINDINGS already flagged for this restaurant. Per the documented precedent, price level alone is grounds to refuse this source even though it is first-party, complete, and prices every item.
notes: Matches a previously-documented case exactly (see FINDINGS: 'A real page with real prices can still be a wrong answer'). Needs a current source -- DoorDash/Yelp/Grubhub listing or a browser -- not another read of the same stale site.

name: El Indio de Tijuana
blocked: Restaurant's own ordering platform is NetWaiter (elindiodetijuanatacoshop.netwaiter.com), address confirmed (810 N Broadway, Escondido). The /escondido/menu route returns byte-identical HTML to the /about route (48412 bytes, a Knockout.js SPA shell) with no embedded menu items or prices -- only cuisine-category and review data are server-side, the actual menu binds client-side with no discoverable JSON endpoint in the served bundle (tried /api/v1/menu and similar guesses, all 404). No DoorDash/Grubhub listing exists -- the restaurant is cash-only with delivery explicitly off. zmenu.com and menupix.com both 403 curl and defeat r.jina.ai (Cloudflare challenge). Yelp 403s a bare curl.
notes: Class of obstacle: needs a browser to watch network traffic on the NetWaiter menu route -- no marketplace or directory alternative exists for this cash-only shop.

name: Melo Melo
notes: melomelo.us is a pure client-side React SPA with nothing server-rendered; grepped the JS bundle (/assets/index-X7YFXxOT_v3.js) for the API host and found manage.melomelo.us/api, which serves /api/products (paginated, 67 total across 7 pages) with per-region price variants keyed by areaId. Confirmed the Southern California areaId (4f788447-15b2-4b98-9600-b360d6e52dd8) via /api/area/initial, and matched the work-list address (4445 La Jolla Village Drive #H17) to the chain's 'UTC' location (4545 La Jolla Village Dr Ste H17, San Diego -- same suite number, same street; the leading digit differs between the two records but the suite match makes this the same store) via /api/locations, which is a chain so all locations share one product catalog and this SC-region pricing applies to all Southern California stores including UTC. Dropped 45 of 67 products: those priced $0.00 (a real gap, not a menu item -- glass mugs, insulated bottles, gift cards, speakers, and several coconut jelly flavors with no price set), everything tagged 'giftset' (merchandise, adjunct), and everything tagged 'coming-soon' (not yet orderable, several of which have a price already staged but are not currently on the menu). Remaining 22 items are the current priced coconut-jelly/tea menu, matching the shop's own description ('desserts, snacks, coconut, or cheese').
